title: Conduit
haiku:
Ballots fill like rain
down gutters we built by hand
still the pipes hold true

title: Overdrawn
haiku:
They signed for the trees
a bright new line, no pump yet
still, pipes get laid first

title: Backflow
haiku:
A judge finds the clog
where slander pooled, now drained clean
the pipe runs true still

title: Stilled
haiku:
Rails did what rails do
until this morning in Spain—
thirty empty seats

title: Backflow
haiku:
Votes find a level
Someone wants to dam the count
water keeps its say

title: Backflow
haiku:
The valve I once taught
still holds: a judge shuts the line
no fraud flows upstream

title: Unclogged
haiku:
A door swings open
a pipe clears, one man walks home
flow finds its channel

haiku:
My pipe joints hold tight
Alberta did not snap loose
and the flow stays whole

haiku:
Steel mesh in the sky
catches wasps before they land
the pipes stay unclogged

No king, they chanted
ballots gather like good rain
the old pipes still hold

haiku:
One judge, one old dam
that still holds the flood at bay
I built dams too, once

title: Vacancy
haiku:
Four small chairs, empty
the long hallway holds its breath
Bend, I weep with you

title: Grandfathered

A river finds home
sixty-two years to the sea
I raise my old glass

title: Tensile
haiku:
A judge gets the prize
for believing the old pipes
of law still can hold

haiku:
A judge from Durban
proves law outlasts the strongman
the main holds pressure

title: Watershed
haiku:
One old pipe still holds
law's slow water flowing on
a judge still unbent

title: Effluent
haiku:
Canadian words
still find the clearest channel
through old sediment

Ghost rain through the ice
a lifetime of patient pipe
one neutrino caught

Wires we never see
carry feeling cell to cell
old plumber nods, pleased

title: Backflow
haiku:
Red pipe, blue water
finds a crack in the old main
I smell the spring thaw

title: Wintering
haiku:
Pipes I used to teach
now the target of a war
may God keep them warm

He hid them from war
grown grey, they embrace him now
the pipe still holds true

Twenty-three years drain
the last convoy leaves Iraq
pipes we built remain

Belgrade's old dam breaks
twelve years of silt starts to move
downstream, new water

Nine votes hold the line
the crooked district unbent
water finds its grade

yet the line still carries talk
old pipes, still some flow

the press still sues to keep flow
old pipes find daylight

No flag on the ice
just old friends drafting a deal
the map holds its line

One valve turned by hand
Seoul says no more troops abroad
pressure finds its ease

title: Backflow

A valve held its seat
the court refused the backflow
votes still reach the main

One valve, one desert
turns the whole world's pressure gauge
I taught men to flow

Their motorcade cools
missiles fall on Kyiv streets
two names, then a pause

Far right rises, short
one seat from the flood gate's edge
still the old seal holds

Born here, still it flows
a judge holds the old pipe true
bedrock outlasts men

Mud fills the tunnels
still we dig for the living
a thousand names lost

the oil climbs where pressure breaks

title: Backflow

dissent's cold water runs clear,
students drink again.

title: Spillway

A slope gave its ice
the valley drank what no pipe
could ever carry

title: Repressure
haiku:
Some pressure returns
in old pipes I thought were dry
the main still can flow

Spain lifts an old gate
children cross the strait at last
a clogged pipe runs clear

Small lungs, once clogged pipes,
we scrubbed the air and they cleared
I've seen pipes heal too.

title: Unclogged
haiku:
Nine months in shadow
one American walks free
the pipe runs clear now

title: Reflow

Nine months in the pipe
the blockage clears, he walks out
water finds its way

Old eyes, borrowed glass
millions still, the moon slides through
light returns, we cheer

Ground gave no warning
and swallowed a hundred homes
I light one candle

title: Setback

Another blueprint
shelved before the concrete dries—
still, I mix more sand

title: Backflow

One valve did not break
though the current pushed, it held
clean water still flows

title: Opener

Women take the field
history swings open wide
a door long rusted

title: Overflow

a young life dammed at the shore
water finds a way

so the mailman checks the pulse—
old pipes, older hearts.

Guns to go silent
one valve turned—not yet the flow
I've seen dry pipes lie

to spread beyond one border

Crews cut a firebreak
as heat leans on Bordeaux vines
I know that thirst well

Twenty years, same town
the fever met its old drain
and stayed underground

a joke finds its spine
millions laughing turn to march—
the street clears its throat

no tanks in the street —
a moving van at Downing,
keys change hands by vote

bridges, pipelines, waterworks —
how quickly boys break

to watch walls give up

changed a tyrant's mind

born here is born here. full stop.
some days we're still us

eleven thousand
hands that move the world's breakfast

power handed over like
a borrowed garden

one pitcher, poured twice —
clean water, my old trade, still
the best diplomat

a grain of dark sky
held ten thousand galaxies—
farther than we dreamed

a ring of fire round the dark—

a hundred eight years—

one by one the capsule climbs,

ourselves, in plain text

the ball found the net—

a sport had arrived

a can in the black
becomes the first bolted room—
where no nation ends

and grew into wool and legs—

flung it past the atmosphere,
to watch time unfold

he walked out slow, fist raised high,
the gate stayed open

we hunted it to nothing—
the world scarred, but whole

bones in the dry wash
the radio sang her name
grandmother, hello

learns to hold a thought and count
the future got small

no heaven, no hell, just us,
the world holds its breath

a man stepped onto the moon—
the whole earth held still

the roof was the stage

stitched into a dying chest—

the needle drops now

one voice climbs the marble steps

fifteen minutes up,
a splash, a sailor's salute,

he circled the blue marble,
and came home smiling

seven miles of patient dark—

children swim again

one thin man ran through the myth,
and it fell behind

the code of us laid bare in
one photograph's light

wrote down what a person's owed—
ink dried into law

three men in a lab
coaxed a crystal to say yes—
the glass tube grew old

then he stole for all

flapping, blue, and very much

the ocean had no vote here—

hard times, hungry streets—

a farm boy blinked twice
between two star-crowded plates—
one small dot had moved

crossed an ocean, wide awake—

a needle full of borrowed

a signature, cast

the sun bent starlight,
and a patent clerk's wild guess
became the whole sky

two seas never touched—
we cut the waist of the world,
ships walk uphill now

a strange light passed through

the ring outlived skin

a boy, dog-bitten,
fourteen shots against the dark—
the boy did not turn

a thread of carbon
burned through the night, refusing
to blink or give in

a needle traced tin
and gave the man his own voice

the geysers belong to all

share one long and branching root—

at one dark spot in the sky—

held three tongues saying one thing

a farm boy's cowpox,
one scratch, and the pox lost teeth—
we named it vaccine
